title: Batching backpressure oscillation: root cause analysis and remediation plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed repeated P99 latency spikes and severe variability on hosted API routes using the continuous batcher. The median latency stayed near target but a subset of requests experienced amplification in tail latency driven by oscillating batch formation and reactive backpressure. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause, short-term mitigations applied during the incident, and a prioritized set of engineering action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-27 09:22 UTC: First alert - P99 for text-generation-route-1 increased from 220ms to 1.8s
2026-02-27 09:30 UTC: Oncall paged, initial triage pointed to batcher saturation and higher queue depths
2026-02-27 09:45 UTC: Temporary mitigation - raised batch formation timer ceiling and enabled fast-path for single-token requests
2026-02-27 10:20 UTC: Latency partially recovered but p99 remained elevated during spike windows
2026-02-27 14:00 UTC: Incident declared over after autoscaling adjustments and routing fallback to smaller model shard pools
2026-03-02: Root cause hypothesis validated with controlled replay of workload in staging
postmortem_summary: Root cause: an interaction between the continuous-batcher debounce logic and our reactive backpressure mechanism produced oscillations in batch sizes during high-mix workloads. Rapid alternation between coalescing and immediate dispatch caused frequent KV cache evictions and uneven GPU kernel utilization. The oscillation created a feedback loop: increased queue depth triggered aggressive backpressure which reduced batch size, which then caused the debounce to restart and build another small batch, repeating until a burst subsided. This amplified P99 and produced fairness issues where long-lived connections accumulated more latency.
technical_root_cause: 1) Debounce timer and backpressure thresholds were tuned statically for homogeneous workloads; they did not account for high-mix short-request bursts. 2) Cache eviction policy lacked awareness of oscillatory batch churn, causing KV cache invalidations for hot prompt prefixes. 3) No upper bound on debounce restart frequency; the system could re-enter coalesce mode multiple times per second for the same connection leading to request thrash.
mitigations: Short-term: implemented a debounce backoff cap and a minimum inter-batch wait for a given connection (deployed 2026-02-27 09:50 UTC)
Short-term: enabled a fast-path that bypasses coalescing for sub-16-token requests when queue depth < 64 (deployed 2026-02-27 10:05 UTC)
Medium-term: adjusted KV cache retention to pin hot prefixes for an additional 30s during oscillatory periods
Long-term: design and implement adaptive coalescing that considers request size distribution and active-connection skew
Long-term: add a backstop that limits debounce restarts per-connection to prevent thrash
Operational: add a dashboard tile showing batch-size oscillation heatmaps per-shard and per-route

follow_up_meeting_notes: 2026-03-04: Cross-team sync - agreed to prioritize adaptive coalescing over heuristic knobs for long-term stability
Discussion: trade-offs between lower debounce latency (better median) vs. throttled restarts (better tail). Decided conservative default to protect P99 for production routes.
Next steps: prototype in staging with traffic replay from 2026-02-27 workload; measure p50/p95/p99 and KV hit-rate
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Chen: Validated root cause in staging by replaying the mixed short/long workload and capturing batch-size time series. Observed identical oscillation when debounce restart frequency was unconstrained.

2026-03-03 - Luca Romano: Prototype for adaptive coalescing started. Using EWMA(window=30s) for avg-token-length and arrival-rate to set target-coalesce-time. Early results show p99 reduction ~35% in staging.
2026-03-05 - Priya Singh: Implemented per-connection cooldown; deploying to canary pool tomorrow. Added unit tests for cooldown logic to ensure we don't stall all connections simultaneously.
2026-03-10 - SRE: Added alert rules and Grafana panels for coalesce-restart-rate and per-shard kv-eviction-rate. Oncall runbook updated.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Park: KV pinning change merged behind feature flag. Observed KV hit-rate improvement during replay, no memory regressions so far. Monitoring for tail-latency regressions continues.
